arxiv-2201-05155.title: Quasiparticle multiplets and 5 f f electronic correlation in prototypical plutonium borides Journal: J. Phys.: Condens. Matter
arxiv-2201-05155.creator: Haiyan Lu, Li Huang
arxiv-2201-05155.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the electronic structures of plutonium borides (PuB x , x x =1, 2, 6, 12) to uncover the fascinating bonding behavior and orbital dependent correlations of 5 f f valence electrons by using the density functional theory combined with single-site dynamical mean-field method.

arxiv-2210-13756.title: Mixed-EVC: Mixed Emotion Synthesis and Control in Voice Conversion
arxiv-2210-13756.creator: Kun Zhou, Berrak Sisman, Carlos Busso, Bin Ma, Haizhou Li
arxiv-2210-13756.description: Abstract Emotional voice conversion (EVC) traditionally targets the transformation of spoken utterances from one emotional state to another, with previous research mainly focusing on discrete emotion categories. This paper departs from the norm by introducing a novel perspective: a nuanced rendering of mixed emotions and enhancing control over emotional expression.

arxiv-2212-05472.title: Surface-induced ferromagnetism and anomalous Hall transport at Zr 2 S(001)
arxiv-2212-05472.creator: Shuyuan Liu 1 , Yanwei Luo 1,2 , Chongze Wang 1 , Hyunsoo Jeon 1 , Yu Jia 3 , and Jun-Hyung Cho 1∗
arxiv-2212-05472.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shuyuan Liu 1 , Yanwei Luo 1,2 , Chongze Wang 1 , Hyunsoo Jeon 1 , Yu Jia 3 , and Jun-Hyung Cho 1∗. Two-dimensional layered electrides possessing anionic excess electrons in the interstitial spaces between cationic layers have attracted much attention due to their promising opportunities in both fundamental research and technological applications. Using first-principles calculations, we predict that the layered bulk electride Zr 2 S is nonmagnetic with massive Dirac nodal-line states arising from Zr-4 d d cationic and interlayer anionic electrons.

arxiv-2311-07421.title: Robust semi-supervised segmentation with timestep ensembling diffusion models
arxiv-2311-07421.creator: Margherita Rosnati, Mélanie Roschewitz, Ben Glocker
arxiv-2311-07421.description: Abstract Medical image segmentation is a challenging task, made more difficult by many datasets’ limited size and annotations. Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM) have recently shown promise in modelling the distribution of natural images and were successfully applied to various medical imaging tasks. This work focuses on semi-supervised image segmentation using diffusion models, particularly addressing domain generalisation.

arxiv-2405-19530.creator: Matteo Buzzegoli, Kirill Tuchin
arxiv-2405-19530.description: Abstract We consider the Dirac field uniformly rotating with angular velocity Ω \Omega and also subject to the constant magnetic field 𝑩 {\bm{B}} directed along the rotation axis. The causal states are constrained to the interior of the light cylinder of radius c / Ω c/\Omega .

arxiv-2406-06704.title: Exploring new constraints on Kähler moduli space of 6d 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 Supergravity
arxiv-2406-06704.creator: Hee-Cheol Kim, and Cumrun Vafa
arxiv-2406-06704.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hee-Cheol Kim, and Cumrun Vafa. We propose new constraints for 6d ( 1 , 0 ) (1,0) supergravity theories based on consistency conditions on the Kähler moduli spaces of their 5d reductions. The requirement that both the metric and the BPS string tensions in the Kähler moduli space are positive imposes specific restrictions on the Chern-Simons coefficients in the 5d effective Lagrangians that are derived from the Kaluza-Klein reductions of 6d theories.

arxiv-2412-02808.title: TCDSG: An End-to-End Approach for Action Tracklet Generation
arxiv-2412-02808.creator: Raphael Ruschel, Md Awsafur Rahman, Hardik Prajapati, Suya You, B. S. Manjunath
arxiv-2412-02808.description: Abstract Comprehensive video scene understanding centers on modeling the temporal evolution of object interactions across frames. Methods that operate framewise often fragment tracklets and break subject–object linkages, limiting long-term activity analysis. We present Temporally Consistent Dynamic Scene Graphs (TCDSG) , a unified end-to-end framework that jointly performs detection, tracking, and interaction linking across video sequences.

arxiv-2508-03784.title: Dynamical dark energy parameterizations in VCDM Preprint: YITP-25-119, IPMU25-0041
arxiv-2508-03784.creator: Simran Arora, Antonio De Felice, Shinji Mukohyama
arxiv-2508-03784.description: Abstract In the context of a theory of minimally modified gravity called VCDM, one can realize any cosmological behavior at the level of the homogeneous and isotropic background without introducing fatal instabilities for perturbations. Therefore, VCDM provides a theoretically-consistent and observationally-testable framework of dynamical dark energy parameterizations with or without phantom behaviors.

arxiv-2508-16579.title: Towards High-Precision Depth Sensing via Monocular-Aided iToF and RGB Integration
arxiv-2508-16579.creator: Yansong Du, Yutong Deng, Yuting Zhou, Feiyu Jiao, Jian Song, Xun Guan
arxiv-2508-16579.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yansong Du, Yutong Deng, Yuting Zhou, Feiyu Jiao, Jian Song, Xun Guan. This paper presents a novel iToF-RGB fusion framework designed to address the inherent limitations of indirect Time-of-Flight (iToF) depth sensing, such as low spatial resolution, limited field-of-view (FoV), and structural distortion in complex scenes. The proposed method first reprojects the narrow-FoV iToF depth map onto the wide-FoV RGB coordinate system through a precise geometric calibration and alignment module, ensuring pixel-level correspondence between modalities.

arxiv-2511-06107.creator: David Kaplan, Nina Jude, Kjorte Harra, Jonas Stampka
arxiv-2511-06107.description: Abstract As of this writing, there are five years remaining for countries to reach their Sustainable Development Goals deadline of 2030 as agreed to by the member countries of the United Nations. Countries are, therefore, naturally interested in projections of progress toward these goals.

arxiv-2601-13448.title: Fairness-informed Pareto Optimization An Efficient Bilevel Framework Thanks: Corresponding author: yassine.laguel@univ-cotedazur.fr
arxiv-2601-13448.creator: Sofiane Tanji ∗, Samuel Vaiter ⋄, Yassine Laguel †
arxiv-2601-13448.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Sofiane Tanji ∗, Samuel Vaiter ⋄, Yassine Laguel †. Despite their promise, fair machine learning methods often yield Pareto-inefficient models, in which the performance of certain groups can be improved without degrading that of others. This issue arises frequently in traditional in-processing approaches such as fairness-through-regularization. In contrast, existing Pareto-efficient approaches are biased towards a certain perspective on fairness and fail to adapt to the broad range of fairness metrics studied in the literature.

pmc-10544488.creator: Mulenga Mary Mukanu, Anne Marie Thow, Peter Delobelle, Zandile June-Rose Mchiza
pmc-10544488.description: BackgroundThe food environment in which people exercise food choices significantly impacts their dietary patterns. Policies that limit the availability, affordability, and access to unhealthy food while increasing that of healthier alternatives help build healthy food environments, which are required to address the double burden of malnutrition. pmc-11294351.title: Air quality forecasting using a spatiotemporal hybrid deep learning model based on VMD–GAT–BiLSTM
pmc-11294351.creator: Xiaohu Wang, Suo Zhang, Yi Chen, Longying He, Yongmei Ren, Zhen Zhang, Juan Li, Shiqing Zhang
pmc-11294351.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The precise forecasting of air quality is of great significance as an integral component of early warning systems. This remains a formidable challenge owing to the limited information of emission source and the considerable uncertainties inherent in dynamic processes. To improve the accuracy of air quality forecasting, this work proposes a new spatiotemporal hybrid deep learning model based on variational mode decomposition (VMD), graph attention networks (GAT) and bi-directional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), referred to as VMD–GAT–BiLSTM, for air quality forecasting.
